# Draft:New Zealand's Heritage: The Making of a Nation

'New Zealand's Heritage: The Making of a Nation' is a serial publication covering the history of New Zealand from earliest occupation up to the 1960s.
Description
This was an extensive publication covering the history of New Zealand from earliest occupation up to the 1960s. The history was published in 105 weekly parts of thirty-two pages each between August 1971 and October 1973, and consisted of text and illustrations both black and white and coloured. The total page count was thus some 2900 and the publisher was Paul Hamlyn Ltd, a New Zealand company. The editor-in-chief was Ray Knox who was assisted by an advisory board consisting of prominent and well-known experts in their field such as; John Beaglehole, Robert Falla, Charles Alexander Fleming, John Grace, Murray Halberg, M. H. Holcroft, Tony McNaughton of the University of Auckland, Guy Powles, John Reid, Angus Ross, Keith Sinclair, Bill Sutch, and Charles Upham. Many of these persons wrote contributing articles. In addition to the weekly parts, binders were made available so that purchasers could amalgamate the series into seven covered volumes.
Reprint
After the initial publication was complete, the whole series was reprinted in twenty-one hard covered volumes and sold as a set.
Follow-up series
In 1973, the same company published a weekly fifteen-part series entitled New Zealand Today, which covered the then current situation in New Zealand. The format was the same as the previous publication.
